p0.en: Key issues: What is the development mandate for children?

p2.original: 先天和后天因素的共同作用帮助儿童掌握重要的发展任务，特别是在语言习得、认知发展和社会关系发展等领域。
p2.en: The combined role of congenital and acquired factors helps children to take over important development tasks, especially in the areas of language acquisition, cognitive development and the development of social relations.

p3.original: 你生命中的三项最大的成就是习得语言、与重要的人建立亲密关系，以及发展思维和推理能力。其中的每一项都是我们后续人生进一步发展的基础。并且，我们将会发现，随着孩子们完成这些任务，他们将经历深刻的心理变化，这些变化是他们的基因代码和环境共同作用的结果。就像核心概念中陈述的本学习阶段的重要观点：
p3.en: The three greatest achievements in your life are the acquisition of language, the establishment of intimate relationships with important people and the development of mental and reasoning capabilities. Each of them is the basis for further development of our lives. And we'll find that as the children do these tasks, they will experience profound psychological changes that are the result of their genetic code and environmental co-effects. Like the important point of view of this learning phase, as set out in the core concept:

p4.original: 先天和后天的共同作用帮助儿童掌握重要的发展任务，特别是在语言习得、认知发展和社会关系发展等领域。
p4.en: The shared roles of the first and the second generation help children to take on important developmental tasks, particularly in the areas of language acquisition, cognitive development and the development of social relations.

p5.original: 儿童和成年人之间的发展差异很大，但是二者在语言、思维和社会化方面的差异，并不仅仅是因为成年人有更多的经验或知识。儿童和成年人之间的差异还包含了成熟过程中关键阶段的逐步展开。换句话说，儿童的能力不仅仅是他们经验的结果，也是他们独特的大脑发育水平的产物。让我们先探索一下那些语言发展的关键阶段。
p5.en: Developments vary greatly between children and adults, but the differences in terms of language, thinking and socialization are not simply due to the fact that adults have more experience or knowledge. The difference between children and adults also involves the gradual development of the critical stages of maturity. In other words, children's abilities are not only the result of their experience, but also the product of their unique level of brain development. Let us first explore the critical stages of those language developments.

p10.original: 7.4 儿童是如何习得语言的

p12.original: 描述儿童语言能力发展的阶段。
p12.en: Describe the stage of child language capacity development.

p13.original: 人类的一个定义性特征是对复杂语言的运用——我们能够通过口语、书面语和手势进行交流。从发展的角度来看，人类语言习得的能力是令人敬畏和振奋人心的：新生儿完全听不懂任何语言，但是短短几年内，所有的孩子都能够流利地运用他们在日常生活中听到的语言，或者他们看到的手语，如美国手语。是什么使他们成为语言学习的行家？发展专家认为，婴儿拥有专门用于这项任务的先天能力（Pinker，1994，2006）。
p13.en: A defining characteristic of humanity is the use of complex languages — we can communicate through words, writings and gestures. From a developmental point of view, the ability of humans to learn the language is apprehensive and inspiring: newborns understand no language at all, but within a few years all children can fluently use the language they hear in their daily lives, or sign language they see, such as American sign language. What makes them masters of language learning? According to development experts, infants have congenital abilities dedicated to this task (Pinker, 1994, 2006).

p15.original: 儿童主要通过模仿他们在所处环境中听到的声音或看到的符号来学习语言的吗？一个著名的理论认为，模仿只能解释儿童学习语言的一部分。在儿童模仿他人语言的背后有一个精细的生物学基础，这个基础使得儿童语言的发展速度远远超过了仅通过模仿所能达到的速度。这个基础是一种先天的心理结构，心理语言学家诺姆·乔姆斯基（Chomsky，1965，1977）称其为语言习得机制（language acquisition device，LAD）。乔姆斯基为我们理解语言发展开辟了新天地，他提出人类在出生时就带有某种心理软件程序，这个程序可以帮助儿童在接触语言时习得词汇、语法和语言规则。很多专家同意他的看法（Hauser et al.，2002）。并且，人类基因组计划（Human Genome Project）的研究证据表明，语言的基础至少部分源于遗传（Liegeois et al.，2001）。
p15.en: Are children learning language primarily by imitating the voices they hear or the symbols they see in their environment? A well-known theory suggests that imitation can only explain part of a child's language learning. A fine biological basis behind the imitation of other languages by children has enabled them to develop their languages at a much faster rate than can be achieved by imitation alone. This foundation is a congenital psychological structure, which is referred to by the psychologist Chomsky, 1965, 1977, as a mechanism for language acquisition (language acquisition device, LAD). Chomsky has opened up a new horizon for our understanding of language development by suggesting that human beings are born with some kind of psycho-software program that can help children learn vocabulary, grammar and language rules when they come into contact with language. Many experts agreed with him (Hauser et al., 2002). Moreover, research evidence from the Human Genome Project indicates that the language base is at least partly genetic (Liegeois et al., 2001).

p16.original: 乔姆斯基的理论认为，LAD或者“心理软件程序”包含了所有人类语言所共有的一些基本规则。规则之一就是区分名词（表示事物的名字）和动词（表示动作）。乔姆斯基指出，这些先天规则使得儿童能更容易地发现他所接触的语言的模式。乔姆斯基理论的另一个支持证据来自一个客观事实：全世界的儿童都在相似的时间内以非常相似的步骤来学习他们的母语。解释一种模式的一个合乎逻辑的假设就是，儿童拥有先天的语言发展“程序”，这个程序会在儿童生命的特定时间点自动运行。
p16.en: Chomsky's theory suggests that LAD or “psychological software program” contains some basic rules common to all human languages. One of the rules is to distinguish between nouns (names indicating things) and verbs (acts expressing things). According to Chomsky, these congenital rules make it easier for the child to discover the pattern of the language he is exposed to. Another evidence of support for the Chomsky theory is derived from the objective fact that children around the world learn their mother tongues at very similar times and in very similar steps. A logical assumption to explain a model is that the child has a “procedure” for the development of an congenital language, which will operate automatically at a specific point in the child's life.

p17.original: 尽管人们普遍认为人类拥有语言习得的先天能力，但是我们也不能忽视环境的作用。虽然婴儿在出生时有能力发出地球上所有语言（大约有4000种）的声音，但是到6个月大时他们的能力似乎被清零了，他们只能发出所处环境中主流语言的声音。在这几个月中，他们听到的声音和他们自己在口头表达中所做的练习，修正了他们努力的方向，因此，他们失去了发出非母语声音的能力。例如，在日语文化中长大的孩子，失去了区分R和L两个字母的语音的能力，因为字母L在日语中是不存在的（Iverson et al.，2003）。
p17.en: Despite the general belief that human beings have the birthright to learn their language, we cannot ignore the role of the environment. While babies are born with the ability to speak all the languages of the planet (about 4,000), by the age of six months they seem to have lost their capacity and to have only the voice of the dominant language in their environment. During these months, the voices they have heard and the exercises they themselves have done in their oral representations have corrected the direction of their efforts and, as a result, they have lost their ability to make non-mother tongue voices. For example, children growing up in Japanese culture lose their ability to distinguish between R and L, because L does not exist in Japanese (Iverson et al., 2003).

p18.original: 儿童语言发展的这种文化差异表明，内置的语言功能并不是一个僵化的装置，而是更像感知语言的一套“收听规则”或指南（Bee，1994；Slobin，1985a，1985b）。婴儿会注意别人说话（或者手语表达）时的声音和节奏，特别是词汇的开始、结束和重音部分。依据内置的“收听规则”，幼儿能快速推断出自己讲话时应该使用的模式和规则。这些现象强调了LAD是灵活的，它能够使幼儿快速适应所处环境中的主流语言（Goldin-Meadow & Mylander，1990；Meier，1991）。
p18.en: This cultural difference in the development of a child's language indicates that the built-in language function is not a rigid device, but rather a set of “rules of listening” or guidelines more like a perceived language (Bee, 1994); Slobin, 1985a, 1985b. The baby is aware of the sound and rhythm of others when they speak (or speak sign language), especially the beginning, end and accent part of the vocabulary. Based on the built-in “rules of listening”, young children can quickly deduce the modalities and rules that they should use when speaking. These phenomena underline the flexibility of LAD, which enables young children to adapt quickly to the dominant language in the environment (Goldin-Meadow & Mylander, 1990); Meier, 1991.

p19.en: 7.4.2 The acquisition of vocabulary and grammar

p20.original: 先天能力是儿童学习语言的基础，但是你认为儿童是如何学习其母语的具体词汇和结构的呢？
p20.en: Inheritance is the basis for children to learn the language, but how do you think children learn the specific vocabulary and structure of their mother tongue?

p21.original: 事实上，他们开始练习语言的时间可能比你了解的还要早。例如，4个月大的宝宝就开始咿呀说话（babbling）：发出重复的音节，例如，“mamamama”。咿呀说话不只是牙牙学语——它是婴儿开始试着构建自己的语言元素。有趣的是，在手语环境中长大的聋儿也会在相同的时间段开始咿呀说话——不过他们是使用双手来模仿美国手语中的重复音节（Petitto & Marentette，1991）。咿呀说话发展得很快，到一周岁时，婴儿进入了单个词的阶段，开始说完整的词语。他们飞快地学习新词，你也许曾注意到“疯狂命名”（naming explosion）这样一个现象，儿童热衷于指着不同的物体并叫出它们的名字。到2岁时，儿童进入能说双词的阶段，这极大地扩展了儿童所能表达的意义的范围。那时，儿童的平均词汇量接近1 000个（Huttenlocher et al.，1991）。到6岁时，这个数量激增到惊人的10 000个（Anglin，1993，1995）。在接下来的数年中，儿童词汇习得的速度进一步加快，如图7-2所示，在很短的时间段内儿童平均可以掌握大约50 000个新词。
p21.en: In fact, they may have started to practice their language earlier than you know. For example, four months old babies start talking (babbling): repeat syllables, such as “mamamamama”. It's not just dental -- it's the baby that starts trying to build its own language. Interestingly, deaf children who grow up in sign language can start talking at the same time - but they use their hands to imitate the repeat syllables in American sign language (Petitto & Marentette, 1991). When I was 1 year old, the baby entered the stage of a single word and began to speak the full word. They learn new words very quickly, and you may have noticed the phenomenon of “naming names”, where children are passionate about pointing at different objects and calling out their names. By the age of two, children enter the dualist stage, which greatly expands the meaning that children can express. At that time, the average number of children's vocabulary was close to 1,000 (Huttenlocher et al., 1991). By the age of six, this number had increased to an alarming 10,000 (Anglin, 1993, 1995). Over the next few years, the pace of the acquisition of child vocabulary has increased further, with an average of 50,000 new words available to children in a very short period of time, as shown in figures 7-2.

p24.original: 熟能生巧 尽管语言的快速发展在很大程度上是由基因设定的时间表决定的，但是文化和环境能够显著影响儿童学习语言的程度和速度。和很多学习任务一样，练习频率的不同会造成学习效果的差异。通常，在孩子年幼时，母亲与女儿说话的量比与儿子的更多（Leaper et al.，1998）。在低社会经济地位家庭和中等社会经济地位家庭长大的孩子之间的差异就更加明显了（社会经济地位是收入和教育水平的综合指标）。在儿童1岁到5岁时，低社会经济地位家庭的父母的平均亲子阅读时间只有25小时，而中等社会经济地位父母的亲子阅读时间可以达到1 000小时（Neuman，2003）。这些早期学习的差异——不仅包括亲子阅读，还包括亲子交流——造成了幼儿园儿童间的巨大差别：来自最贫困家庭的儿童在5岁时的标准语言测试中其成绩要落后两年，他们的词汇量只有接受更多语言刺激的儿童的一半（Hoff，2013）。
p24.en: While rapid language development is largely determined by genetic time frames, culture and environment can significantly influence the extent and speed with which children learn languages. As with many learning assignments, differences in the frequency of practice can result in differences in learning outcomes. In general, mothers talk more to their daughters than to their sons when their children are young (Leaper et al., 1998). The difference between children growing up in low- and middle-income households is even more pronounced (socio-economic status is a composite indicator of income and educational attainment). In the case of children aged 1 to 5, the average reading time for parents of families with low socio-economic status is only 25 hours, while the average reading time for parents of parents with medium-economic status is 1,000 hours (Neuman, 2003). These differences in early learning, which include not only reading by parents but also communication by parents, result in a significant difference among children in kindergarten: children from the poorest families lag two years behind in standard language tests at the age of five, and their vocabulary is only half as much as those who receive more language incentives (Hoff, 2013).

p25.original: 语法将词汇转化为语言 相同的单词按不同的顺序进行组合可以表达不同的含义。例如，“我看见他在追狗”和“我看见狗在追他”使用了相同的词，但是互换他和狗两个字的顺序就可以表达完全不同的意思。是语法（grammar）造成了这一差异：这是一套语言规则，将词汇进行组合和排序创造出人们可以理解的句子（Naigles，1990；Naigles & Kako，1993）。不同语言可能会使用完全不同的语法组合规则。例如，在日语中，动词通常被放在句尾，而英语中动词的位置相对而言就随意多了。如果你也会说西班牙语，你就知道，“蓝色的房子”在英语中的表达是“the blue house”，而在西班牙语中表示颜色的词会放在名词后面（la casa azul）。
p25.en: Syntax translates the vocabulary into a language, and the same words are combined in different order to express different meanings. For example, “I saw him chasing a dog” and “I saw a dog chasing a dog after him” used the same word, but the order of the words interchanged between him and the dog could mean a completely different meaning. It is the grammar (grammar) that causes this difference: it is a set of language rules that combines and ranks words to create understandable sentences (Naigles, 1990); Naigles & Kako, 1993. Different languages may use completely different grammatical combination rules. For example, in Japanese verbs are usually placed at the end of the sentence, while in English verbs are relatively randomly located. If you speak Spanish, you know that the word “blue house” in English is “the blue house” and the word “colour” in Spanish is placed behind the word (la casa azul).

p26.original: 第一句话 在儿童早期的双词或三词句子中，儿童使用的是一种电报式语言（telegraphic speech）。例如，“要饼干”就是电报式语言。为了培养组成整句的能力，儿童必须学会使用其他的言语形式。例如，修饰语（形容词和副词）和冠词（the，that），他们还必须学会如何使用语法把单词组合起来。在英语中，这意味着识别和生成熟悉的主语-谓语-宾语这一顺序，例如，“小羊跟着玛丽”（The lamb followed Mary）。
p26.en: The first sentence, in two or three sentences in the early years of the child, is a telegraphic language. For example, “crackers” is a telegraphic language. In order to develop the capacity to make up the whole sentence, children must learn to use other forms of speech. For example, qualifiers (adjectives and adjectives) and crowns (the, thet) must also learn how to combine words using syntax. In English, this means identifying and generating the order of familiar principals - the term - the bean, for example, “The lamb followed Mary”.

p27.original: 最后，随着儿童语言能力的发展，他们开始熟练地使用语素（morpheme），语素是组成单词的单个意义单元。例如，单词“unmarried”（未婚）有3个语素：“un”“marry”和“ed”。与之相似，“subcategories”（亚类们）也有3个语素：“sub”“category”和“es”。语素可以为动词标记时态（walked，walking），也可以为名词标记所有格（Maria's，the people's）和复数形式（foxes，children）。（你能说出这些例词的语素数量吗？）但是，儿童经常会犯错误，因为他们不知道规则或者不会恰当地运用规则（Marcus，1996）。一个常见的错误叫作过度规则化（overregularization），是指扩大了规则的使用范围，从而创造出不正确的单词形式。例如，在知道过去时态就是在动词后面加-d或-ed之后，儿童会将这一“规则”运用到不规则动词上，创造出一些假词，例如，“hitted”和“breaked”。在学会用-s或-es创造复数形式后，儿童会将这一规则用到不规则名词上，如“foots”和“mouses”。
p27.en: Finally, with the development of the language skills of children, they have begun to use the grampheme (morphemé), which is the single meaning unit that forms the word. For example, the word “unmarried” has three synonyms: “un” “marry” and “ed”. Similarly, “subcategories” (subcategories) have three words: “sub” “category” and “es”. Textures can be used to mark verbs in the current state (walked, walking) or to mark all cells (Maria's, the people's) and complex forms (boxes, children). Can you give me the linguistics of these words? However, children often make mistakes because they are unaware of the rules or do not properly apply them (Marcus, 1996). A common error, known as overregularization, refers to the expansion of the use of the rule and thus the creation of incorrect word forms. For example, after knowing that the past has been followed by a verb -d or -ed, children would apply this “rule” to irregular verbs, creating a number of pseudonyms, such as “hitted” and “breaked”. After learning to create a plural form of -- s or -- es, children will use this rule in irregular terms, such as “foots” and “mouses”.

p29.original: 学习词汇以及组合词汇的语法规则仅仅是有效交流的开端，儿童还需要学习交流的社交规则。他们必须学习如何加入讨论，如何轮流说和听，以及如何做出相应的贡献。成年人会使用身体语言、语调和面部表情来增强交流效果。他们还会对倾听者的反馈做出回应，也经常可以从倾听者的角度进行思考和回应。儿童必须掌握这些技能才能成为一个成功的交流者，这反过来又使得他们成为人类语言社会的一分子。
p29.en: Learning vocabulary and the grammar rules of combinations are only the beginning of effective communication, and children also need to learn social rules of communication. They must learn how to join the discussion, how to speak and listen in turn, and how to contribute accordingly. Adults use body language, tone and facial expression to enhance communication. They also respond to the feedback of listeners and can often think and respond from the perspective of listeners. Children must acquire those skills in order to become successful communicators, which in turn makes them part of the human linguistic community.

p30.original: 随着儿童长大，他们也学会了表达抽象的意思，特别是当他们的想法超出了物理世界而进入他们的心理世界时。例如，2岁之后，儿童开始使用类似做梦、忘记、假装、相信、猜和希望等词语来谈论自己的内部心理状态（Shatz et al.，1983）。他们也使用高兴、伤心和生气等词语来表达自己的情绪状态。随着认知能力的进一步发展，他们能够理解和使用诸如真相、正义和想法等高度抽象的词语。
p30.en: As children grow up, they learn to express abstractions, especially when their ideas go beyond the physical world and enter their psychological world. For example, after the age of two, children begin to use terms like dream, forget, pretend, believe, guess and hope to talk about their internal psychological state (Shatz et al., 1983). They also use the words of joy, sadness and anger to express their emotional state. As cognitive capacity further develops, they can understand and use highly abstract terms such as truth, justice and ideas.

p31.original: 在复杂的语言习得过程中要突出的主要观点是什么呢？那就是我们下述核心概念的一部分：语言是儿童期的一项主要发展任务——儿童为此做了精心的准备。儿童习得和使用语言的方式表明，在长大成人的道路上的这些早期步骤既依赖于先天的时间表，也依赖于环境的刺激。
p31.en: What are the main points to be highlighted in the complex process of language acquisition? That is part of our core concept that language is a major development task in childhood — for which children are carefully prepared. The way children learn and use their language suggests that these early steps on the path to adulthood depend on both congenital timetables and environmental incentives.

p32.original: 7.5 认知发展：皮亚杰的理论

p34.original: 解释皮亚杰的认知发展理论。

p35.original: 如果你曾注意到学步期的儿童会进入一个“疯狂命名”的阶段，那么你一定看到过儿童乐此不疲地对他们认识的物体进行命名。这种命名背后是他们的思维、知觉和记忆能力逐渐开始发展。接下来的内容将关注这些心理能力是如何形成的：这个过程被称为认知发展（cognitive development），它是我们核心概念所定义的儿童期的三个主要发展任务中的第二个。
p35.en: If you've noticed that children in school are going to enter a phase of “crazy naming”, you must have seen children be happy to name objects they know. Behind this naming is the gradual development of their mental, sensory and memory abilities. The next section will focus on how these mental capacities are formed: this process is called cognitive development, which is the second of the three main developmental tasks of childhood as defined by our core concept.

p36.original: 认知发展领域的心理学家试图回答以下这些问题：
p36.en: Psychologists in the field of cognitive development have tried to answer these questions:

p37.original: 儿童是在何时意识到，即使他们看不见物体了，物体也依然存在？
p37.en: When did children realize that even if they could not see objects, they would still exist?

p38.original: 他们知道自己的想法可能是不正确的吗？
p38.en: Do they know they might be wrong?

p39.original: 他们是否能够理解人类拥有愿望和梦想，但是物体没有这些？
p39.en: Can they understand that human beings have aspirations and dreams, but not those things?

p40.original: 正如瑞士心理学家让·皮亚杰（Jean Piaget）在他的开创性研究中所做的那样，发展心理学家不仅研究儿童思考的内容，也研究儿童思考的方式。在近50年的时间里，皮亚杰专注观察儿童的智力发展，并将他的观察建构成一个综合性理论。
p40.en: As Jean Piaget, a Swiss psychologist, did in his pioneering study, developing psychologists studied not only the content of children's thinking but also the way in which they thought. For nearly 50 years, Piajé has focused on observing the intellectual development of children and has constructed his observations into a comprehensive theory.

p41.original: 通过仔细观察自己的3个孩子的行为，皮亚杰开始了他对儿童心理的探索。他的方法很简单：他会向他们出问题，然后观察他们的反应，再稍微改变一下情景设置，然后再一次观察他们的反应。皮亚杰特别关注孩子们的思维、推理和问题解决等能力的发展性转化和改变。这种关注促使皮亚杰提出了发展的阶段理论（stage theory）。这个理论强调，在儿童期和青少年期，人们的思维加工方式会经历独特的变革，这一过程可以分成4个分离的阶段。随后我们将讲述皮亚杰理论中的3个关键概念：
p41.en: By looking closely at the behaviour of his three children, Piajji began his psychological exploration of children. His approach was simple: he would ask questions about them, then look at their reactions, then change the scenario a little bit, and then look at their reactions once. Piage is particularly concerned with the developmental transformation and transformation of the capacities of children, such as thinking, reasoning and problem resolution. This concern prompted Piajer to propose a phase-by-stage theory of development. The theory emphasizes that in childhood and adolescence, people experience unique changes in ways of thinking, a process that can be divided into four separate stages. Then we will talk about three key concepts in Piajj's theory:

p44.original: 3. 认知发展阶段（stages of cognitive development）。

p46.original: 为了解释图式这个概念，请想象一些四条腿的动物；现在，请想象一些友好的动物；接着，请想象一种会吠叫的友好的动物。你可能首先会想到大象、老虎、猫和狗（都是四条腿动物），然后你的选项可能会缩小为猫和狗（有四条腿并且友好），最后你的选择只剩下狗（它会吠叫）。你很容易就能完成这个任务，因为你已经发展出了能使你理解概念和事件的心理结构。皮亚杰用术语“图式”来命名这些心理结构。我们拥有概念的图式，如“狗”和“发展”。我们也有动作的图式，如“用筷子吃饭”或“学习”。我们也有解决问题的图式，如“计算圆的面积”和“安抚一个正在哭闹的宝宝”。一般来说，图式是指导思维的心理框架。根据皮亚杰的解释，图式也是发展的基本组成部分。当我们发展和组织我们的知识体系以接受新的体验或者预测将来的事件时，就会形成新的图式或改变旧的图式。当你读到这里时，你正在构建一个关于图式的图式！
p46.en: In order to explain the concept of the pattern, imagine some four-legged animals; Now, imagine some friendly animals; Then imagine a friendly animal that barks. You might think of elephants, tigers, cats and dogs first, and then your options could be reduced to cats and dogs (with four legs and friendly), and in the end, only dogs. It is easy for you to accomplish this task, because you have developed a psychological structure that enables you to understand concepts and events. Piajer named these psychological structures using the term “map”. We have conceptual patterns, such as “dogs” and “development”. We also have action patterns, such as "eating with chopsticks" or "learning." We also have problem-solving patterns, such as “calculating the area of the circle” and “preventing a crying baby”. In general, the diagram is the psychological framework that guides thinking. According to Piage, the chart is also an essential component of development. When we develop and organize our knowledge systems to receive new experiences or predict future events, new or old patterns are created. When you read here, you're building a pattern!

p47.original: 同化和顺应 在皮亚杰的理论系统中，所有的认知发展都基于两个动态过程：同化和顺应。同化是将新的信息、情境或者例子整合到现有图式中的一个心理过程。因此，一个知道怎么抓手摇铃的婴儿会将相同的策略应用到抓住照料者的首饰上。同样，家里养有金丝雀的年龄稍大的孩子去动物园时，可能也会运用同化过程明白体型更大的鹦鹉或火烈鸟也是鸟类。当你看到你最喜欢的演员的新电影信息时，或者当你使用你计算机上的某个程序的新版本时，你也在经历同化这一过程。本质上，同化过程就是我们将新信息整合进一个现有图式从而扩展这一图式。
p47.en: In the theoretical system of Piajje, all cognitive development is based on two dynamic processes: assimilation and adaptability. Assimilation is a psychological process to integrate new information, situations or examples into the existing pattern. Thus, a baby who knows how to grab a bell will apply the same strategy to the jewelry of a caregiver. Similarly, older children with canaries in their homes may also use assimilation processes to understand that larger parrots or flamingos are also birds. When you see your favorite actor's new movie information, or when you use a new version of a program on your computer, you're also going through the process of assimilation. In essence, the assimilation process is one that expands the pattern by integrating new information into an existing pattern.

p48.original: 相反，当新信息不能很好地匹配现有图式时，我们就使用顺应。顺应是重建或修正图式以接纳新信息的过程。因此，一个学会抓手摇铃和首饰的儿童可能会在以相同的方式抓一个大球时遇到困难。与之类似，如果一个小孩在第一次去动物园时看到了一只蝙蝠，她将需要为“蝙蝠”创造一个新图式，因为它是一种有翅膀但又不是鸟的生物。成年人也会体验到他们心理图式的顺应。例如，互联网使很多人对购物和交流这两个概念的图式进行了顺应。作为一个学生，当你使用的学习方法不能让你获得理想的成绩时，你有时候可能需要修正你的学习图式。
p48.en: On the contrary, when new information does not match the current pattern well, we use it accordingly. Corresponding should be the process of re-establishing or amending the pattern to accommodate new information. As a result, a child who learns to ring his hands and jewellery may encounter difficulties in catching a ball in the same way. Similarly, if a child sees a bat on her first visit to the zoo, she will need to create a new pattern for the bat, because it is a creature with wings but not birds. Adults also experience their psychological responses. For example, the Internet has enabled many people to adapt to the two concepts of shopping and communication. As a student, you may sometimes need to revise your learning patterns when the learning methods you use do not allow you to achieve the desired results.

p49.original: 顺应也能帮助你适应不同的文化和习俗。例如，即使在美国，不同文化中的交流规则也是不同的。如果你的交流图式中包含了两位发言者之间要有一个礼貌的停顿，然后你又恰巧进入了一个拥有打断和互相讨论的图式的群体，那么你会发现你插不上话。因此，你不得不顺应（改变你原有的交流图式）以适应新环境。在我们日益多元化的世界里，顺应可能是适应新环境的一种非常有效的策略。
p49.en: Adaptation can also help you adapt to different cultures and customs. Even in the United States, for example, the rules of communication vary across cultures. If your communication pattern includes a polite pause between the two speakers, and then you happen to be in a group with a pattern of interruptions and discussions, then you find yourself out of touch. So you have to adapt to the new environment. In our increasingly diverse world, adaptability can be a very effective strategy for adapting to the new environment.

p50.original: 婴儿发现奶瓶和乳房一样都可以吸吮，因此，她进行了同化过程，她将吸吮一个瓶子加入自己现有的吸吮图式中。
p50.en: The baby found that the bottle was as good as the breast, so she had an assimilation process, and she would suck a bottle into her existing suction pattern.

p51.original: 皮亚杰认为，认知发展是同化和顺应不断交替出现的结果。通过这两个过程，个体的行为和知识会逐渐减少对具体的外部现实环境的依赖，并增加对内部思维的依赖。一般来说，如果新信息整合进现有图式，你是在同化；但是当你为了新信息必须改变你的图式或创造一个新图式时，你则在顺应（见图7-3）。
p51.en: Piage believes that cognitive development is the result of the constant alternation of assimilation and adaptability. Through both processes, individual behaviour and knowledge can gradually reduce dependence on specific external realities and increase reliance on internal thinking. In general, if new information is integrated into the existing pattern, you are assimilating; But when you have to change your pattern or create a new one for new information, you are responding (see figures 7-3).

p52.original: 图7-3 同化和顺应，区别是什么
p52.en: Figure 7-3 Assimilation and adaptability, what the difference is

p54.original: 你生活中的同化和顺应
p54.en: The assimilation and adaptability of your life.

p55.original: 想一想你最近的一段新体验。例如，开始在新学校学习，开始一份新工作，参加某种新活动，或者任何其他包含了某些不熟悉的元素的东西。在那段经历中，你先前的哪些知识经验可以迁移到新情境中，以帮助你更快地适应新情境（同化）？你是否最终不得不为新情境创建一个图式（顺应）？如果是的话，现在请你写下来。
p55.en: Think about your latest experience. For example, it begins to study in new schools, to start a new job, to participate in a new activity, or anything that contains certain unfamiliar elements. In that experience, what of your previous knowledge and experience could be migrated to a new context to help you adapt more quickly to the new context (assimism)? Did you finally have to create a pattern for the new situation (responsive)? If so, please write it down now.

p56.original: 7.5.2 皮亚杰的认知发展阶段
p56.en: 7.5.2 The cognitive development phase in Piajé

p57.original: 现在我们了解了图式，以及它们是如何不断地被新信息塑造的，接下来让我们开始探讨在儿童发展过程中皮亚杰观察到的儿童知觉世界的4个革命性变化。他把这些变化描述为认知发展的阶段：
p57.en: Now that we have learned how the images are shaped and how they are constantly shaped by new information, let us begin by looking at the four revolutionary changes in the consciousness of children observed by Piajay in the process of child development. He describes these changes as the stage of cognitive development:

p58.original: 1. 感觉运动阶段（sensorimotor stage，婴儿期）；

p59.original: 2. 前运算阶段（preoperational stage，儿童早期）；

p60.original: 3. 具体运算阶段（concrete operational stage，儿童中期）；
p60.en: 3. Specific operating stages (concrete operational status, mid-child);

p61.original: 4. 形式运算阶段（formal operational stage，青春期）。
p61.en: 4. Form computing phase (formal operational stage, adolescence).

p62.original: 随着儿童从感觉反应到逻辑思维的不断进步，每个阶段都有新的思维方式涌现。最值得注意的是，成熟过程决定了所有儿童都以相同的顺序经历这4个阶段。虽然遗传约束依然起作用，但是由于遗传和环境的交互作用，某些孩子会更快地通过某个阶段。例如，相比于教育资源匮乏的儿童，在教育资源丰富的环境中成长的儿童会更快地掌握每个阶段的认知任务。
p62.en: As children move from feeling to logical thinking, new ways of thinking emerge at every stage. Most notably, the maturity process determines that all children go through these four stages in the same order. Although genetic constraints still function, some children pass some stage faster because of the interaction between genetic and environmental interactions. For example, children who grow up in resource-rich environments are better equipped with the cognitive task of each stage than children who lack the resources for education.

p63.original: 感觉运动阶段（出生到2岁） 我们已经了解到，儿童来到这个世界时已经拥有了许多天生的感觉能力和反射行为，如识别熟悉的声音、抓握和吸吮反射。根据皮亚杰的理论，感觉运动阶段的儿童主要通过这些感觉和运动行为来探索世界。例如，他们学会将感觉到的信息和他们的运动能力协调起来，如学习转头看身后的物体；然后，如果他们想要这个物体，他们就会爬向它或者走过去。皮亚杰将其称为感觉运动智力（sensorimotor intelligence）。
p63.en: We have learned that children come to this world with many instinctive abilities and reflexes, such as recognizing familiar voices, seizing and sucking reflections. According to Piajje, children in the sensory stage are primarily exploring the world through these feelings and sporting behaviour. For example, they learn to reconcile perceived information with their motor capabilities, such as learning to look behind objects; And then if they want this object, they'll climb to it or they'll walk. Piage called it sensory motor intelligence.

p64.original: 在这个快速发展的阶段，婴儿努力达成的主要成就是客体永久性（object permanence），它在婴儿8个月大时开始出现。你可能曾注意到，在这个时期之前，婴儿不会寻找一个不见了的玩具或者其他物体。皮亚杰对此的解释是，婴儿不知道当他们看不见一个物体时它还是存在的。换句话说，婴儿认为看不见的东西就不存在了。然而从8个月大开始，如果你给婴儿看一个玩具，然后你当着他的面把玩具藏到了毯子下面，那么他就会到毯子下面去寻找这个玩具。甚至，当藏东西和找东西之间间隔了一分钟或更长的时间时，婴儿也会毫不犹豫地这样做。这表示婴儿开始理解客体永久性。在接下来的数月中，婴儿寻找物体的能力不断增强，他们能够在更长时间间隔后寻找物体，也能够更顺利地找到与第一次所藏的位置不同的物体（Moore & Meltzoff，2004）。
p64.en: At this stage of rapid development, the main achievement of the infant effort is permanent (object permanence), which began to emerge when the baby was eight months old. You may have noticed that before this time, babies would not be looking for a missing toy or other object. Piage explained that the baby did not know it existed when they could not see an object. In other words, what the baby thinks is invisible doesn't exist. But from the age of eight months, if you show the baby a toy, and you hide it under the blanket in front of him, he'll go under the blanket and look for it. Even when there is a minute or more between hiding and searching, babies do not hesitate to do so. This means that the baby begins to understand the purpose of perpetuity. In the following months, babies have been able to find objects with increasing capacity to search for objects at longer intervals and to find objects at a different location from the first cache (Moore & Meltzoff, 2004).

p65.original: 客体永久性可以帮助我们理解分离焦虑（separation anxiety）。任何照顾过婴儿的人肯定都曾注意到，当你离开婴儿时，婴儿会变得非常烦躁不安——这在客体永久性早期是相当常见的。毕竟，他们还不明白你还会回来的。相反，婴儿觉得，当你离开房间时，你就消失不见了。想象一下，这对于婴儿来说是多么恐怖的事！（你可以在前一部分有关依恋的描述中了解到分离焦虑的行为表现，当婴儿的母亲离开房间时，婴儿变得烦躁不安。）一旦儿童完全理解了客体永久性（这标志着感觉运动阶段的结束），儿童就可以理解，即使他们看不见某个人或某个物体，这个人和这个物体仍然存在。这使得大部分儿童可以在2岁左右开始摆脱分离焦虑。
p65.en: It's not like the time has come for us to be able to understand the separation anxiety. Anyone who has taken care of a baby must have noticed that when you leave the baby, the baby becomes very restless — it is quite common in the early years of the permanent body. After all, they don't know you're coming back. Instead, the baby felt that when you left the room, you disappeared. Imagine how horrible it is for a baby! (You can learn from the description of attachment in the previous part of the act of separating anxiety, when the mother leaves the room, the baby gets restless. Once the child fully understands the permanent nature of the object (which marks the end of the sensory phase), the child can understand that even if they do not see an individual or an object, that person and that object still exist. This has enabled most children to begin to escape separation anxiety at around the age of two.

p66.original: 在取得这些成就的同时，婴儿也在学习目标导向行为（goal-directed behavior）。这可以从他们用各种物体进行的实验中得到证据。例如，不小心把勺子掉在地上的儿童，可能对勺子从地砖上弹起时发出的啪嗒声非常感兴趣，然后他就一遍一遍地重复这个动作。听觉敏感的旁观者可能觉得这非常烦人，但是对于婴儿而言，他只是在高兴地练习如何控制自己的世界！
p66.en: These achievements are accompanied by the learning of targeted behaviour (goal-directed behavior). This can be demonstrated by their experiments with various objects. For example, a child who accidentally dropped a spoon on the ground may be very interested in the sound of a spoon when it starts to pop from the bricks, and then repeats it over and over again. Audience-sensitive bystanders may find this very annoying, but for babies, he's just happy to practice how to control his own world!

p67.original: 客体永久性的出现连同婴儿越来越多的目标导向行为，表明婴儿开始形成有关物体的心理表征（mental representation）以及婴儿认识到他们自己和世界之间的关系。这种心理表征增强了婴儿的思维能力和问题解决能力。在婴儿早期只能即时出现的模仿行为将变得可以延时出现，这就是观察学习（observational learning）的开始。6个月大的婴儿可以模仿他前一天看到的行为；到2岁时，他们可以保留和模仿一个月前看到的行为（Klein & Meltzoff，1999）。这些感觉运动阶段的成就推动幼儿进入下一个阶段：前运算阶段。
p67.en: The presence of permanent objects, together with the increasing number of targeted behaviours of infants, indicates that babies begin to form psychological manifestations of objects and that babies are aware of their own relationship with the world. This psychological manifestation increases the mental capacity of the baby and the ability to solve problems. The only instant imitation that occurs at an early stage of an infant will become available over time, and this is the beginning of observational learning. A six-month-old baby can imitate the behavior he saw the day before; By the age of two, they can retain and imitate the behaviour seen a month ago (Klein & Meltzoff, 1999). The achievements of these sensory stages drive young children into the next phase: the pre-calculation phase.

p68.original: 前运算阶段（从2岁到7岁） 这是第二个发展阶段，在此阶段儿童的认知发展表现在对物体的心理表征能力的发展上。在注意到感觉运算阶段的飞速发展之后，皮亚杰似乎将前运算阶段视为感觉运算阶段和第三个阶段（具体运算阶段）之间的过渡阶段。在他的观察中，这个阶段是将感觉运动阶段出现的符号能力进行扩展和巩固的时期。因此，他将这个阶段的主要特征描述为对儿童思维的限制，而不是发展。让我们来探讨一下其中的一些特征。
p68.en: The pre-calculation stage (from 2 to 7 years of age) is the second stage of development, at which the cognitive development of children is reflected in the development of the psychological expression of objects. Having noted the rapid development of the sensory phase, Piajer seems to see the former operating phase as a transition between the sensory phase and the third phase (the specific operating phase). In his observation, this phase is a period of expansion and consolidation of symbolic capabilities that emerge during the sensory phase. He therefore described the main features of this phase as constraints to children's thinking, not development. Let us explore some of these features.

p69.original: 自我中心主义（egocentrism）使得儿童只从自己的角度来看待这个世界。并且他们认为，其他人也会以相同的方式来看待这个世界。（需要补充的是，皮亚杰并没有将自我中心主义看作自私，而仅看作儿童看待世界的一种有限视角。）皮亚杰通过“三山任务”的实验[1]发现了这一现象。因此，当你在电话里跟前运算阶段的儿童交谈时，他可能只是用点头（没有说话）来回答你的问题，并且他也不会留意到你看不见他点头。另一个自我中心主义的有趣例子是儿童觉得他遮住了眼睛就没人能看见他了！皮亚杰认为，由于这种自我中心主义，前运算阶段的儿童不能对他人感同身受，也不能站在他人的角度思考问题。这是皮亚杰理论有争议的部分，我们稍后会详细说明这一点。
p69.en: Self-centeredness has made children view the world from their own perspective. And they think that others will look at the world in the same way. (It needs to be added that Piajé does not see self-centreism as selfish, but rather as a limited view of the world for children. Piage discovered this phenomenon through the experiment of the Three Mountain Mission [1]. So when you talk to the children in the pre-calculation phase on the phone, he's probably just nodding his head to answer your questions, and he won't notice you can't see him noding. Another interesting example of self-centreism is that children think that they can't see him if they're blind! Pierje believes that, because of this self-centreism, children in the pre-calculation stage cannot feel the same way about others, nor can they think from the perspective of others. This is a controversial part of Piajer's theory, and we will elaborate on it later.

p70.original: 泛灵论思维（animistic thinking）是指儿童相信非生物体也和人类一样具有生命和心理过程。因此，我们看到儿童会与泰迪熊玩过家家，会给掉在地上的布娃娃贴创可贴，或者担心修剪树枝会伤到树木。
p70.en: Animism thinking refers to children's belief that abiotics also have life and psychological processes as human beings. Thus, we see children playing home with Teddy Bears, putting stickers on the dolls that fall on the ground, or worrying about cutting branches and hurting trees.

p71.original: 中心化（centration）是指儿童的注意范围过于狭窄而错失了其他重要信息；也就是说，儿童一次只能“集中”于非常少的信息。这会导致儿童不能理解事情或者问题的“全貌”。例如，一个口渴的小孩坚持要喝“大杯”果汁，他会选择细长的杯子而不是矮宽的杯子，虽然两者的容量是一样的。在前运算阶段儿童的心里，玻璃杯越高，装的果汁就越多，但是他们没有注意到另一个杯子更宽。从前运算阶段进入具体运算阶段的一个标志是从中心化过渡到守恒（conservation）（见图7-4）。
p71.en: (a) Centralization refers to children's too narrow attention and missing other important information; In other words, children can only “focus” on very little information at a time. This can lead to children not being able to understand the “full picture” of the matter or the problem. For example, a thirsty child insists on a “big” juice, and he chooses a thin glass instead of a short one, although both have the same capacity. The higher the glass, the more the juice is in the mind of the children at the pre-calculation stage, but they do not notice that the other glass is wider. A sign of the transition from centralization to continuity (see figure 7-4) is the transition from the former to the specific operating phase.

p73.original: 注：前运算阶段的儿童在思考的时候一次只能注意到事物的一个特征——在这个例子中，就是高或者矮。他们不能同时注意到宽度的差异，也就不能理解当液体从一个容器倒入另一个形状不同的容器时液体的总量保持不变。
p73.en: Note: Children at the pre-calculation stage can only think of one characteristic at a time - in this case, high or short. They cannot at the same time note the differences in width or understand that the total quantity of liquid remains the same when the liquid falls from one container to another in a different shape.

p74.original: 不可逆性（irreversibility）是指儿童不能在想清楚解决问题包括的一系列事件或步骤后，再反转这一过程，逆推回到心里的起点。简言之，前运算阶段的儿童缺乏大一些的孩子所具备的心理试错能力，即在头脑中完成一个动作然后撤销这个动作的能力。例如，山姆看到玛利亚把一盒葡萄干洒在桌上，因为葡萄干摊开来的面积很大，山姆就在心里想：“哇！玛利亚的葡萄干比我的小盒子里的多。”但是前运算阶段的山姆不能够在心里逆推这个过程，然后想：“如果她把所有的葡萄干装回盒子里，那么她的葡萄干和我盒子里的葡萄干就是一样多的。”这种能力的缺乏是前运算阶段儿童进行逻辑思考的最大障碍。
p74.en: Irreversibility means that a child cannot reverse the process and reverse the beginning of the mind when he or she has thought clearly of the series of events or steps to address the problem. In short, children in the pre-calculation stage lack the mental error skills of a larger child, that is, the ability to complete an action in their mind and then to reverse it. For example, Sam saw Maria spill a box of raisins on the table because of the size of the raisins, and Sam was like, "Wow! Maria has more raisins than in my box. But Sam at the pre-calculation stage couldn't reverse the process in his heart, and he thought, "If she put all the raisins back in the box, her raisins were just as many as those in my box. This lack of capacity is the biggest obstacle to children's logical thinking at the pre-calculation stage.

p75.original: 虽然皮亚杰将这些视为局限性，但是我们认为更重要的是要明确在此期间哪些能力得到了发展。儿童正在试验他们新获得的心理表征能力，在这个过程中，他们非常具有创造力。我们从他们展现出的泛灵论思维中看到了创造力，也从其他“过家家”式的假扮游戏中看到了创造力，后者是前运算阶段的一个核心特征。事实上，我们可以认为，在下一个阶段，当问题解决中的创造力下降时，这种“进步”不仅仅是一种收获，从某些角度看也是一种损失。
p75.en: While Piajer sees these as limitations, we believe that it is more important to clarify which capacities have been developed during this period. Children are experimenting with their newly acquired psychological manifestations, and in the process they are very creative. We see creativity in their panthematic thinking, as well as in other “pass home”-style games, which are a central feature of the pre-calculation phase. In fact, we can assume that this “progress” is not just a gain, but a loss from some point of view, at the next stage, when creativity is declining in the solution of the problem.

p76.original: 具体运算阶段（从7岁到11岁） 在这个阶段中，儿童突破了不可逆性的阻碍，第一次明白了即使很多东西的外观发生了变化，本质仍然保持不变。在具体运算阶段，他们可以理解矮宽的玻璃杯和细长的玻璃杯装的果汁一样多，也能理解撒出来的葡萄干还可以装回盒子里。在掌握守恒概念的过程中，曾经难倒前运算阶段儿童的问题已不复存在，取而代之的是儿童对体积守恒方式的新的理解。与之类似，他们现在也能理解一串红珠子并没有比相同的一串蓝珠子多，即使红色的珠子排成一行，而蓝色的珠子混成一团。他们已经认识到虽然看起来珠子组织在一起的方式不一样，但这并不意味着它们的数量不一样。
p76.en: During this period of concrete computing (from 7 to 11 years of age), children break through irreversible barriers and for the first time realize that, even though many things have changed in their appearance, their nature remains unchanged. At the specific operating stage, they can understand that as much as a small glass and a thin glass of juice can be filled, and that the raisins that are spilled can be put back in the box. In mastering the concept of continuity, the problem of children at the pre-calculative stage has ceased to exist and has been replaced by a new understanding of the way in which they maintain their size. Similarly, they now understand that a string of red beads is not more than the same string of blue beads, even if the red beads are lined up and the blue beads are lumped together. They have realized that, while it seems that beads are organized in different ways, this does not mean that they are not in the same number.

p77.original: 除了有理解守恒的能力，这个阶段的儿童还有一项奇妙的新能力。儿童可以通过完全在头脑中运用概念来解决问题，这被心理学家称为心理运算（mental operation）。这使得具体运算阶段的儿童可以在采取行动之前进行思考。这样，他们就不会冲动行事了。他们也不会那么容易上当受骗，不再相信一些“奇妙”的事，如圣诞老人或牙仙子，他们现在知道这些都是不存在的。
p77.en: In addition to the capacity to understand persistence, children at this stage have a wonderful new capacity. Children can solve problems by using concepts exclusively in their minds, which are referred to by psychologists as psychological calculations. This allows children at the specific operational stage to think before action is taken. In that way, they would not be impulsive. Nor would they be so easily deceived, and no longer believe in “magic” things, such as Santa Claus or the Tooth Fairy, which they now know do not exist.

p78.original: 因此，具体运算阶段的儿童开始运用简单的推理来解决问题。然而，他们在推理中使用的符号仍然主要是具体的事物或事件，而不是抽象符号。通过知名的“20问”游戏可以展示出儿童具体思维的局限性。这个游戏要求玩家通过提出尽可能少用“是或不是”这样的词进行回答的问题来猜测出另一个人心里想的物体。这个阶段的儿童通常会提出一系列具体的猜想（是鸟吗？是猫吗？），而不能提出更高水平的关于类别的问题来有效地缩减正确答案的范围（它会飞吗？它有毛吗？）。
p78.en: As a result, children at the specific operating stage began to use simple reasoning to solve the problem. However, the symbols they use in their reasoning are still primarily specific things or events, not abstract symbols. The limitations of children's specific thinking can be demonstrated through the well-known “20 questions” game. This game requires the player to guess what another person thinks by asking questions that are answered with as few words as possible, such as “yes or no”. Children at this stage usually offer a series of specific conjectures (birds? Is it a cat? Instead of raising a higher level of questions about categories to effectively reduce the scope of the correct answer (does it fly? Does it have hair? I don't think so.

p79.original: 我们将把对皮亚杰认知发展的最后一个阶段——形式运算阶段——的讨论留到青春期部分进行。现在，我们简单介绍一下，最后一个阶段中关于抽象思维发展的内容。表7-2总结了皮亚杰提出的四个阶段。
p79.en: We will leave the discussion on the last stage of Piajé's cognitive development — the form calculation phase — to the adolescent segment. Now, let us briefly describe the last phase of the development of abstract thinking. Table 7-2 summarizes the four phases proposed by Piajje.

p82.original: 大部分心理学家都接受了皮亚杰所描绘的认知发展的概貌（Beilin，1992；Lourenço & Machado，1996）。然而研究人员发现，每个阶段的儿童在某些方面的表现都比皮亚杰所认为的更加复杂（Munakata et al.，1997）。
p82.en: The majority of psychologists have received a picture of cognitive development as depicted by Piajé (Beilin, 1992); Lourenço & Machado, 1996. However, researchers have found that children at every stage perform in some ways more complex than Piajé believes (Munakata et al., 1997).

p83.original: 能力出现的时间早于皮亚杰理论的相关线索 有时候，处于感觉运动阶段或前运算阶段的儿童，可以掌握皮亚杰所认为的在该阶段他们不能掌握的能力。客体永久性就是一个例子：心理表征早在婴儿4个月的时候就出现了，而不是皮亚杰所认为的2岁左右。给4个月的婴儿展示“可能”或“不可能”的事件时，婴儿不会对“可能”的事件表现出惊讶，但是会在看到“不可能”事件时表现出惊讶（Baillargeon & DeVos，1991；见图7-5）。
p83.en: Capabilities have emerged earlier than the relevant clues to Piage's theory, and sometimes children at the sensory or pre-calculation stage have the ability that Piage believes they cannot have at that stage. One example is the permanent nature of the object: psychological symptoms appear as early as four months before the baby, rather than about two years of age, as Piage thought. When showing “possibly” or “unlikely” events to a four-month-old baby, the baby would not be surprised by the “possibly” event, but would be surprised to see the “unlikely” event (Baillargeon & DeVos, 1991); See figures 7-5.

p84.original: 研究人员还发现，与皮亚杰的中心化概念相反，四岁的儿童可以理解物体的看不见的内部（如鸡蛋、橡皮球或狗的内部）可能和它的外观不一样（Gelman & Wellman，1991）。并且，与皮亚杰的泛灵论思维不一致的是，当要求3岁到5岁的儿童做迫选任务时，他们可以区分真实的物体和纯心理（想象）的物体（Wellman & Estes，1986）。最后，关于自我中心主义，到4岁时，儿童就能经常从他人的视角看事物：相比于与大孩子和成年人聊天，他们在与2岁儿童交谈时会使用更简单的语言、更短的单词，这一事实说明了这一点（Gelman & Shatz，1978）。总体而言，皮亚杰对4个阶段顺序的观察是正确的，但是今天的儿童发展某些认知技能的速度似乎比皮亚杰所观察到的要更快。
p84.en: The researchers also found that, contrary to Piajer's concept of centralization, children as a 4-year-old can understand that the invisible internals of objects (such as those of eggs, rubber balls or dogs) may differ from their appearance (Gelman & Wellman, 1991). Moreover, in contrast to Piajé's aesthetic thinking, when children between the ages of 3 and 5 are required to perform an forced selection, they can distinguish between real objects and purely psychological (imaginative) objects (Wellman & Estes, 1986). Finally, with regard to self-centreism, children are often able to see things from the perspective of others when they reach the age of four: this is illustrated by the fact that they use simpler language and shorter words when they talk to children of two years of age than they do with older children and adults (Gelman & Shatz, 1978). Overall, Piajje is right to observe the sequence of four phases, but today children seem to be developing some cognitive skills faster than Piajje has observed.

p90.original: 心理理论 这些认知能力的提升标志着心理理论（theory of mind）的发展，心理理论是指个体理解他人可能拥有与自己不同的信念、愿望和情绪，并且这些心理状态会影响那个人的行为（Frith & Frith，1999）。你的心理理论决定了你期望他人在某个特定情境（如当他收到礼物时或者是当他被骂时）下做何反应。重要的是，心理理论包括了我们认识到我们对他人行为的期望，需要根据我们对这个特定个体的了解而进行调整。这种对他人心理世界的理解促进了我们对他人的同情心，也使我们学会骗人，并且在关键时刻还会增加我们对他人做出正确判断的机会。
p90.en: The mental theory, which is a sign of the development of theory of mind, refers to the individual's understanding that another person may have different beliefs, aspirations and emotions and that these mental states influence the behaviour of that person (Frith & Frith, 1999). Your psychological theory determines how you expect others to react in a particular situation (e.g. when he receives a gift or when he is abused). Importantly, psychological theory includes an awareness of what we expect from others and needs to be adapted to our understanding of this particular individual. This understanding of the psychological world of others promotes our compassion for others, it also enables us to learn to lie and, at a critical juncture, it increases the opportunity for us to make the right judgement about others.

p91.original: 最近的证据显示，这些能力可能早在婴儿6个月大时就出现了——这与我们前文讨论的客体永久性的最近研究发现相吻合。一项研究发现，6个月大的婴儿就能够准确地区分能带来帮助的人和带来危险的人，并且他们始终会选择能带来帮助的人作为自己的玩伴（Hamlin et al.，2007）。感觉运动阶段和前运算阶段的认知成就促进了这一内在能力的进一步发展，到5岁时，不同文化下的儿童都可以理解他人对世界的看法可能与自己不同（Callaghan et al.，2005）。要了解儿童心理理论的有趣案例，请上网搜索视频“回心转意”（A Change of Mind），来看看你是否能找到心理理论的例证，以及皮亚杰的前运算阶段思维方式的一些例子。然后，请回答以下问题：
p91.en: Recent evidence suggests that these capabilities may have emerged as early as six months of age — consistent with the findings of recent studies on the permanent nature of the object that we discussed earlier. A study found that a six-month-old child can accurately distinguish between those who can bring help and those who are at risk, and that they always choose those who can help to play with themselves (Hamlin et al., 2007). The cognitive achievements of the sensory and pre-calculation phases have contributed to the further development of this inherent capacity, and by the age of five, children of different cultures can understand that others may see the world differently from themselves (Callaghan et al., 2005). For an interesting case of child psychology, please search the video "A Change of Mind" to see if you can find examples of psychological theory and some examples of how Piajé has been thinking at the pre-calculation stage. Then please answer the following questions:
